findings.title: The trial button gives no terms, and nothing on the page backs up the promise

location.description: the "Start a 30-day trial" button, and the empty space below the features

findings.viewer_experience: A small-shop owner can read "30-day trial" as a free month or as a first paid month, and the wrong reading stops the click. Nothing compares Shelfmark with how the owner works now or shows a price or a named shop, and the "Pricing" and "Shops using it" nav items point to nothing on the page.

current.value: the button says only "Start a 30-day trial", with no terms under it and no comparison, price or named shop on the page

findings.target: One line of trial terms directly under the button, and a comparison with the owner's current way of knowing what to reorder, plus the price or a named shop, in the empty lower part of the page.
findings.fix_direction: Put the trial terms in one line directly under the button. Then use the empty lower part of the page for a comparison with the owner's current way of knowing what to reorder, plus the price or a named shop. Only the maker has these facts: whether the trial is free or paid, whether a card is needed, what happens after day 30, the price, and a real shop. The maker must supply them.

closed_when.check: In the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen images, a fresh critic sees a line of trial terms directly under "Start a 30-day trial", and a comparison with the owner's current method plus a price or a named shop on the page.

findings.title: The tablet hero paragraph and feature lines run past 75 characters per line

location.description: the hero paragraph under the headline on the tablet

findings.viewer_experience: The lines are too long to track from one line to the next.

current.value: 94 characters per line in the hero paragraph; 79, 87 and 59 in the feature lines

findings.target: 75 characters per line or fewer, with the text measure capped at about 600 px and the table at full width
findings.fix_direction: Cap the text measure at about 600 px, or give the paragraph a max-width, while the table stays at full width.

closed_when.check: characters_per_line of div.hero-text > p and section.facts > p in the tablet viewport is 75 or less

findings.title: The phone table headers and one title wrap onto two lines

location.description: the "On shelf" and "Sold this week" table headers on the phone

findings.viewer_experience: The header row and the "Notes from the Ferry" row are taller than the others, so the table looks uneven.
findings.target: each table row on one line
findings.fix_direction: Shorten the headers on narrow screens ("Sold this week" could become "Sold") or narrow the cell padding, so each row stays one line.

closed_when.check: lines of thead > tr > th:nth-of-type(2), thead > tr > th:nth-of-type(3) and tbody > tr:nth-of-type(4) > td:nth-of-type(1) in the phone viewport is 1

findings.title: The reorder table has no order-quantity column

location.description: the header row of the "Reorder this week" table

findings.viewer_experience: The table says what to reorder but not how many copies, so the owner cannot act on it.

current.value: three columns: Title, On shelf, Sold this week

findings.target: an order-quantity column if the product suggests a quantity; otherwise the maker confirms it does not and the table stays as it is
findings.fix_direction: If the product suggests a quantity, show it. If it does not, the maker should confirm that and the table stays as it is. Only the maker knows whether the product suggests a quantity.

closed_when.check: In the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen images, the table shows an order-quantity column, or the maker has confirmed the product suggests no quantity.
